content.title: Line Cut to Word | Material Response and Readable Hold
content.summary: A first sparse line operation produces a material effect; additional line actions physically change the same substrate so a readable original word emerges from its geometry, followed by a deliberate title hold and new ending state.

quick_start.input_format: Begin with one visible line operation on a stable material surface, with no fully formed title yet. + Later line operations cause bounded physical material changes that accumulate into legible negative or positive letter geometry. + Hold the resulting original word long enough to read and give it a deliberate ending state.
quick_start.recommended_input: A cold translucent ice monolith in a blue studio has four pre-scored, self-supporting letter-core shapes concealed within the block. Three amber thermal seams successively unlock the small connecting bridges, letting the cores fall into a clear tray and revealing the original open-form word 'LIFE' in through-cavities; the surrounding outer frame remains intact.

creative_dna.mechanism: A first sparse line operation produces a material effect; additional line actions physically change the same substrate so a readable original word emerges from its geometry, followed by a deliberate title hold and new ending state.

invariants.rule: Begin with one visible line operation on a stable material surface, with no fully formed title yet.
invariants.purpose: Makes the first intervention and baseline readable.
invariants.ablation_failure: Starting with the word removes the material-to-type reveal.

invariants.rule: Later line operations cause bounded physical material changes that accumulate into legible negative or positive letter geometry.
invariants.purpose: Connects graphic motion to object construction.
invariants.ablation_failure: If letters simply fade in, the line actions become decorative and causal coherence disappears.

invariants.rule: Hold the resulting original word long enough to read and give it a deliberate ending state.
invariants.ablation_failure: A blurred or instantly shattered word fails as a title, even if material effects look impressive.

slots.name: material
slots.constraint: One stable original substrate with consistent physical properties.

slots.name: line_operation
slots.constraint: Sequential visible marks/cuts/unpicking actions, first one before title.

slots.name: bounded_change
slots.constraint: Only affected material changes at each line.

slots.name: letter_formation
slots.constraint: Readable new word emerges from physically traceable result.

slots.name: title_hold
slots.constraint: Final typography readable, not random glyphs.

slots.name: ending_state
slots.constraint: Purposeful resolution distinct from copied source explosion.

slots.name: sound
slots.constraint: Original material-specific sounds, not source audio attribution.

anti_copy_exclusions: No weapon/titanium wall, bright orange metal sparks, source word 'BLADE', exact metal fragment choreography or terminal blast.
Do not copy the live-page creator prompt or treat it as hash-bound canonical prompt evidence.
No sudden after-effect text overlay that ignores the earlier material operations.

instantiations.prompt_seed: Cold blue ice monolith, three bounded thermal seams unlock concealed letter cores, negative-space LIFE remains intact.

instantiations.concept: A tactile woven stage cloth carries one cream thread under tension; three successive unpicking pulls free connected stitch runs and reveal a hidden contrasting weave spelling the original word 'HOME'; the cloth relaxes and folds gently rather than shattering.
instantiations.prompt_seed: Handwoven cloth, sequential unpicking of cream thread, underlying weave reveals HOME, soft final fold.

failure_modes.failure: Text appears as an unrelated overlay before the material moves.
failure_modes.repair: Track the same pieces or negative-space cavity from each line to letters.

failure_modes.failure: Cuts occur everywhere at once and obscure the first cause.
failure_modes.repair: Give one clear first mark, then separate later operations.
Reserve an unobstructed stable legibility hold before a controlled ending.

failure_modes.failure: A closed glyph leaves a floating unsupported center or missing removed material.
failure_modes.repair: Use open-form letters; show pre-scored letter cores and their physical descent into a visible tray.
